title: coder: resolve and trust portable program and question packages
body:
<!-- openagents-project-triage:start -->
## Project triage

Project: [Coder as Decision Router Consumer](https://github.com/orgs/OpenAgentsInc/projects/16) · Workstream: Portable programs · Priority: P2 · Readiness: Blocked.

Parent tracker: #9501.

Open prerequisites linked with native **blocked by** relationships: #9495, #9488, #9470.

Local lock/trust resolution can ship first. Full remote-catalog integration needs the relay/public discovery and catalog owners; discovery never grants execution permission.

<!-- openagents-project-triage:end -->

---

Make Coder consume discoverable program/question/capability packages without turning discovery into executable authority.

Specification: [portable program registry](https://github.com/OpenAgentsInc/openagents/blob/main/docs/coder/coder-as-decision-router-consumer.md#portable-program-registry). Consumer tracker: #9501. Service tracker: #9481.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Define a versioned package/lock record for program, question, source, policy, and capability references with content digests, provenance, publisher identity, dependencies, and compatibility requirements.
- [ ] Resolve local files first; add authenticated remote discovery/import through the supported public and relay catalogs. Verify digests and publisher trust before accepting updates.
- [ ] Keep fetch/inspect separate from installation and execution. An imported package cannot approve its own probe, grant credentials, enable hosted disclosure, or widen filesystem/network access.
- [ ] Provide explicit update/diff/rollback and offline cache behavior; pin the package for the lifetime of a run and refuse unresolved or incompatible dependencies.
- [ ] Allow programs to use approved HTTP/local/relay capabilities while keeping machine-specific executable paths and secrets outside portable manifests.
- [ ] Test tampering, stale/replaced advertisements, untrusted publishers, cyclic dependencies, revoked approval, and offline resolution.

## Dependencies and boundaries

#9470/#9488/#9495 own discovery/catalog publication; this issue owns Coder's resolver and trust boundary. Existing capability-trust approvals remain authoritative.

Product code remains Rust; reuse the repository's shared contracts and manual/non-GitHub verification. This issue describes planned work, not implemented behavior.
